GN1.r: Classical mechanics with unrestricted probability distributions is exactly the simplex theory - the fully classical GPT.

GN2a.r: Adding a knowledge-balance (epistemic) restriction on top of classical mechanics generates Spekkens' toy theory.

GN2b.r: The same epistemic restriction on continuous (Liouville) mechanics reproduces Gaussian quantum mechanics exactly - states, dynamics and quadrature statistics.
GN2b.c: Uncertainty-saturating Gaussian restriction, cell set by hbar.

GN2c.r: The same construction on discrete Z_d phase space reproduces the odd-d stabilizer subtheory; Gross's nonnegative Wigner function is that model, and it is the unique noncontextual one.

GN3.r: No epistemic restriction of any classical theory can reproduce the qubit stabilizer subtheory - the construction provably fails at even dimension.
GN3.c: Even d; state-independent contextuality is the obstruction.

GN4.r: Full quantum mechanics arises from classical mechanics by deforming the Poisson bracket into the Moyal bracket; an exact (undeformed) lift is impossible beyond quadratic observables.

GN5.r: The deformation terms beyond the Poisson bracket (order hbar^2, active only for anharmonic dynamics) are precisely what generates Wigner negativity - and with it CV contextuality.
GN5.c: Quadratic Hamiltonians keep Moyal = Poisson, so the Gaussian world stays positive. Derived assembly.

GN6.r: Choosing complex amplitudes is what buys local tomography: composite states are fixed by local statistics over C, but not over R.

GN7.r: The imaginary unit makes i[A,B] an observable, so observables close under commutation and coincide with generators of dynamics - the quantum Noether link.
GN7.c: Fails in real QM without superselection workarounds.

GN9.r: hbar sets the size of the epistemic cell: the classical uncertainty area defining the restriction that generates Gaussian QM.
GN9.c: Scale-setting role, not a structural axiom.

GN10.r: Sending hbar to 0 contracts the Moyal bracket back to Poisson and the state space to a simplex - the classical limit as deformation shutdown.

E12.r: No-signalling plus 'every mathematically valid effect is physical' generates boxworld - the maximal nonlocal theory, whose extremal correlations are PR boxes.

E13.r: Separable quantum theory is defined by the minimal tensor product, and that choice provably breaks purification: mixed separable states have no pure extension inside the theory.

MH1.r: Quantum theory contains entangled states - the PSD cone strictly exceeds the separable cone - giving the first hop of the generative route to Bell violation.
MH1.c: d_A, d_B >= 2; continue via B2 (pure states) plus B7 (incompatible measurements).

MH2.r: Gaussian QM contains entangled states (two-mode squeezing), but which witnesses they fire depends entirely on the probing process: steerable with quadratures, Bell-blind under Gaussian measurements.

MH3.r: The odd-d stabilizer subtheory contains genuinely entangled states that nevertheless admit a local, noncontextual model - entanglement without contextuality.
MH3.c: Restricted to stabilizer measurements; the key counterexample to reading 'entangled' as 'contextual'.

MH4.r: Boxworld contains entangled states: PR boxes are entangled elements of the maximal tensor product, giving CHSH = 4 despite trivial dynamics.
MH4.c: Max tensor product of square state spaces.

R1.r: If two noninteracting systems have a nondegenerate total spectrum, every time-symmetric joint state is classical-classical: no discord, no entanglement, no steering, no Bell. Symmetric quantum correlations can only live inside degeneracy blocks.
R1.c: H = H_A + H_B with all level sums distinct; degenerate blocks (equal-gap qubits) escape. Generated edge, round 3.

R2.r: All time-symmetric measurements are mutually compatible - each is a coarse-graining of the energy measurement - so symmetric probes can never show incompatibility, steering or Bell violation.

R3.r: Some entangled states violate no Bell inequality at all, yet their steering-based sequential scenario is still contextual: contextuality detects composite nonclassicality that Bell tests provably miss.
R3.c: Werner LHV region; the contextual fragment uses ALL measurements on the steered side. Generated edge, round 3 (composition A8 with B3).

R4a.r: A magic state can carry no correlations at all (|T> tensor |0> is a pure product state): magic does not imply discord.

R4b.r: A discordant state can be entirely stabilizer-made: discord does not imply magic. With R4a, magic and discord are logically independent clusters.
R4b.c: Counterexample with commutant proof; generated, round 3.

R5.r: The KD analogue of Hudson's theorem: which pure states have classical (nonnegative) KD distributions is fixed by support-uncertainty conditions; mere noncommutation is not enough for negativity.
R5.c: Pure states; DFT bases give the sharp rule n_A x n_B = d. Literature fill, round 3.

R6.r: Gaussian and odd-d stabilizer epistricted theories can show no third-order interference - they inherit I3 = 0 from quantum theory. For the toy field theory nothing fixes I3: genuinely open.
R6.c: Inheritance holds only for quantum subtheories; the toy theory is not one (gap SG4). Generated, round 3.

A1.r: Incompatible measurements exist exactly when the state space is not a simplex: incompatibility and nonclassicality are the same boundary.

A2.r: Universal broadcasting (copying all states) is possible exactly in classical theory; every nonclassical GPT has a no-cloning theorem.

A3.r: A classical system cannot be entangled with anything - its composites are all separable; and whenever BOTH systems are nonclassical, some valid composite contains entanglement. Classicality holds iff entanglement is impossible.
A3.c: 'Can be entangled', not 'must be': the minimal tensor product stays consistent (see E13/F3).

A4.r: Nonclassicality, superposition (strong incompatibility) and entangleability are one and the same property of a pair of theories; superposition alone already powers BB84.

A5.r: A fragment has a noncontextual explanation exactly when it fits inside a simplex (states) and its dual (effects): contextuality = failure of simplex embedding.
A5.c: Prepare-measure fragments; a finite linear-program test exists.

A6.r: Contextuality is the same thing as unavoidable negativity: a fragment is noncontextual iff SOME nonnegative quasiprobability representation of it exists.
A6.c: Negativity of one chosen representation proves nothing by itself (see C8).

A7.r: A contextual system is automatically entangleable: contextuality forces a nonsimplicial cone, which forces beyond-minimal composites to contain entanglement.
A7.c: Derived (P1); converse fails - the toy theory is entangleable yet noncontextual.

A8.r: Entanglement cannot exist without contextuality nearby: certifying entanglement makes the derived sequential scenario contextual, and entanglement witnesses map to noncontextuality inequalities.
A8.c: Remote-state-preparation mapping; all measurements available on the steered side.

A9.r: A fragment can be broadcast exactly when it has a noncontextual model: no-broadcasting and contextuality are the same operational boundary at fragment level.

A10.r: Incompatibility neither produces nor is needed for contextuality: noncontextual theories can have incompatible measurements, and contextuality can be proven with fully compatible (even a single) measurement.
A10.c: Counterexamples both ways; contrast the conditional A11.

A11.r: But if ALL quantum states are available as preparations, then incompatibility, steerability and contextuality do coincide.

B1.r: Bell violation is strictly stronger than steering: every Bell-violating assemblage steers, not conversely.

B1b.r: Steering is strictly stronger than entanglement: separable states always admit a local-hidden-state model.

B2.r: Every PURE entangled state violates some Bell inequality (Gisin's theorem).

B3.r: Mixed entangled states can be fully Bell-local: Werner states have local models for all single-copy measurements, POVMs included.

B4.r: With trusted quantum inputs (semiquantum games), every entangled state outperforms all separable ones.
B4.c: Quantum inputs replace classical setting choices.

B5.r: Bell-locality of a state can be undone: local filtering or many copies can activate hidden nonlocality.

B6.r: An assemblage steers exactly when the steering party's measurements are incompatible - steering and incompatibility are two faces of one resource.

B7.r: Compatible measurements can never violate Bell; any incompatible PAIR of dichotomic measurements can, with the right state - but larger incompatible SETS may still fail to.

B8.r: Whether undistillable entangled states with negative partial transpose exist is open since 1998 - the distillability problem.
B8.c: PPT implies undistillable is proven; the converse is the question.

B9.r: Bound entanglement can still violate Bell inequalities: the Peres conjecture (PPT implies local) is false.

B10.r: Every entangled state is detected by SOME witness operator - but no efficient universal detector can exist, because deciding separability is NP-hard.
B10.c: Completeness via Hahn-Banach; hardness grows with dimension.

B11.r: Deciding membership in the quantum correlation set is not just hard but undecidable (MIP* = RE); the set is not even closed.

B12.r: Bell violation is the operational fuel of device-independent randomness and key distribution.

B13.r: Steering powers one-sided device-independent QKD: only one lab needs to be trusted.

B14.r: For multiqubit systems, Kochen-Specker contextuality cannot be shown without entanglement: logical proofs need entangled measurements, statistical ones entangled states.

B15.r: Bell and KS scenarios translate into each other: an invertible map carries contextuality proofs to nonlocality proofs and back.
B15.c: Structural bridge, not identity of resources.

B16.r: In combined scenarios, contextuality and nonlocality trade off against each other - a monogamy forced by no-disturbance.

C1.r: In odd prime dimensions, a state can violate a stabilizer noncontextuality inequality exactly when its Wigner function goes negative: negativity = state-dependent contextuality there.

C2.r: The same equivalence holds in continuous variables: Wigner negativity and contextuality coincide for quadrature-displacement measurements.

C3.r: A nonnegative Wigner function makes the computation classically simulable, so negativity is necessary for quantum speedup in these settings.

C4.r: Magic states are the fuel that promotes free stabilizer circuits to universal quantum computing.

C5.r: The odd-d stabilizer world is noncontextual, and its classical explanation is essentially unique: Gross's Wigner representation, which equals the epistricted model.

C6.r: The qubit stabilizer world admits NO nonnegative explanation at all - it is contextual in every even dimension, state-independently (Mermin square).

C7.r: Generalized contextuality is a necessary resource for universal quantum computation by state injection - in all dimensions.
C7.c: Also powers MBQC and shallow-circuit advantages.

C8.r: Warning edge: a clever nonnegative hidden-variable model covers even universal quantum computation - negativity is representation-relative; only contextuality (negativity in EVERY representation) is invariant.
C8.c: The model is not diagram-preserving, so no contradiction with C5-C7.

C9.r: KD negativity, in the right experimental scope, implies contextuality - it forces negativity in every representation.
C9.c: Scope caveats once generalized KD representations are allowed.

C10.r: An anomalous weak value is by itself a proof of contextuality.

C11.r: KD negativity buys metrological advantage: anomalously large postselected Fisher information.

C12.r: Preparation contextuality is exactly what powers the quantum advantage in parity-oblivious multiplexing.
C12.c: The optimal advantage saturates the contextuality bound.

C13.r: Contextuality gives a quantifiable advantage in minimum-error state discrimination.

C14.r: Any state-independent KS proof converts into an inequality every state violates; state-dependent violations start at d = 3 and need a non-chordal compatibility graph.

D1.r: Inside quantum theory, coherence converts to entanglement: incoherent operations plus an incoherent ancilla turn basis coherence into entanglement, bounded by the input coherence.

D2.r: No coherence, no contextuality: a fragment diagonal in one basis is simplex-embeddable, so every contextuality proof needs basis-independent coherence somewhere in it.

D3.r: Coherence is not enough: epistricted theories show superposition structure and all textbook two-path interference while staying noncontextual.

D4.r: There is no coherence threshold: contextuality can be witnessed with arbitrarily little coherence - the amount is not the resource.

D5.r: Unspeakable coherence and asymmetry are the same notion: coherence across conserved-quantity eigenspaces is exactly noninvariance under the symmetry group.
D5.c: Group generated by the conserved quantity.

D6.r: Real-amplitude quantum theory is experimentally false: network Bell tests separate complex from real QM - the imaginary unit is physical.
D6.c: Entanglement-swapping networks; single-site statistics cannot separate them.

E1.r: No-signalling alone permits stronger-than-quantum correlations: PR boxes reach CHSH = 4.
E1.c: Hence extra principles are needed to recover quantum.

E2.r: Information causality caps correlations at the quantum Tsirelson bound - but whether it carves out exactly the quantum set is open.

E3.r: Macroscopic locality caps correlations at NPA level 1 - close to, but strictly above, the quantum set.

E4.r: Local orthogonality (the exclusivity principle) rules out PR boxes and recovers the exact quantum bound of the KCBS inequality.

E5.r: The almost-quantum set obeys the main device-independent principles yet fits NO theory with the no-restriction property - reproducing it forces a restriction on measurements.

E6.r: Purification is the entanglement-forcing axiom: every mixed state having a pure extension yields entanglement, steering, teleportation and no-cloning - and with five informational axioms, quantum theory itself.

E7.r: Boxworld buys maximal nonlocality at the price of trivial dynamics: no entanglement swapping, no teleportation by dynamics.
E7.c: Its reversible dynamics are only local operations and permutations.

E8.r: Local quantum structure plus no-signalling composition already caps bipartite correlations at the quantum set: Tsirelson's bound is a ceiling theorem, not a source of violations.
E8.c: The generative route to Bell runs through states and measurements (MH1, then B2/B7).

E9.r: Quantum theory has exactly second-order interference: the Sorkin parameter I3 vanishes identically; higher-order theories (density cubes) exist but are not quantum.

E10.r: Any nonclassical theory that can decohere to classical must contain entanglement: emergent classicality needs entanglement.
E10.c: A decoherence map onto a classical subtheory is assumed.

E11.r: Reading the quantum state as mere knowledge fails: preparation-independent psi-epistemic models contradict quantum statistics (PBR), and maximal psi-epistemicity fails for d >= 3.
E11.c: Each no-go needs its stated assumption; fully unrestricted psi-epistemic models do exist.

F1.r: Spekkens' toy theory imitates a long list of quantum phenomena - incompatibility, no-cloning, interference, steering ensembles, teleportation analogues - while staying local and noncontextual: imitation phenomenology proves nothing by itself.

F2.r: Gaussian QM steers (two-mode squeezing) but cannot violate Bell with Gaussian measurements, and the whole subtheory has a classical epistemic model: steering without contextuality.

F3.r: Separable quantum theory keeps single-system negativity, magic and contextuality while containing zero entanglement - the burden of entanglement lies on the composition axiom, not the local structure.

F4.r: Boxworld violates information causality, macroscopic locality and local orthogonality - PR boxes trivialize communication complexity.

F5.r: Real-amplitude QM breaks local tomography: joint states of real systems are not fixed by local measurements.

G1.r: Under thermal operations a whole family of free energies (all alpha-Renyi) must decrease - many second laws, not one.

G2.r: Energy coherence is a thermodynamic resource of its own: covariance of thermal operations forbids creating it and forces it to decay - constraints beyond all free energies.
G2.c: Time-translation covariance of the free operations.

G3.r: Work-locking: the coherent part of free energy is NOT extractable as work from a single system without a phase reference.
G3.c: Unlocks collectively or with an ancillary reference.

G4.r: Anomalous work and heat statistics witness contextuality: fluctuation setups reproducing classical two-point statistics either carry a work quasiprobability or fail on contextual protocols - and that quasiprobability's negativity certifies contextuality.

G5.r: Initial quantum correlations can push heat from cold to hot - the thermodynamic arrow bends, as observed in NMR experiments.

G6.r: In sharp theories with purification, thermodynamics is well-posed and purity is DUAL to entanglement - the entanglement-thermodynamics duality is not specifically quantum.

G7.r: A bipartite state can be locally broadcast exactly when it has zero discord: discord is the obstruction to local copying.

H1.r: Superposition alone - in any nonclassical theory - suffices to run BB84 key distribution.

H2.r: Incompatibility is exactly the resource behind quantum advantage in random access codes.

H3.r: Contextuality quantifies the advantage in entanglement-assisted one-shot classical communication.

I1.r: OPEN: no known set of device-independent principles singles out quantum correlations; the almost-quantum set survives them all.

I2.r: OPEN: no quantitative bridge from coherence amount to contextuality strength is known.
I2.c: Gap G2; proposed LP sweep of fragments.

I3.r: OPEN: the odd-d 'negativity = contextuality' equivalence has no qubit counterpart; what measure plays that role for qubit magic?
I3.c: Gap G3; the ZOR model obstructs naive versions.

I4.r: OPEN: which composites admit steerable states - the steering analogue of entangleability of cones?

I5.r: OPEN: is every contextual process visible in some thermodynamic statistic (work, heat, entropy production)?
I5.c: Gap G4; N1 forces probes off the TTS cluster.

I6.r: OPEN: contextuality quantifiers for higher-order-interference theories are uncharted; the density cubes' status is unknown.

I7.r: OPEN: which thermodynamic requirements FORCE purification-type axioms - the converse of GPT thermodynamics?

I8.r: OPEN: a general monogamy calculus between single-system contextuality and composite nonlocality is missing.

I9.r: OPEN: the thermodynamic signature of bound entanglement is uncharacterized.

I10.r: Contextuality is testable in practice: a linear program on accessible fragments, robust to noise, detector inefficiency and (with care) tomographic incompleteness.

S1.r: An entangled state is coherent in EVERY product basis - being diagonal in any product basis already means separable.
S1.c: Coherence is basis-relative; every state is diagonal in its own eigenbasis, so claims must name the basis.

S2.r: Entanglement implies discord on both sides: zero-discord states are automatically separable.

S3.r: Thermal states are a subcluster of time-symmetric states ([gamma, H] = 0).

S4.r: Energy coherence IS asymmetry under time translation (unspeakable coherence) - quantified by asymmetry monotones, not by populations.

S5.r: Wigner negativity implies magic in odd dimensions - but not conversely: bound magic states are Wigner-positive yet non-stabilizer.

S6.r: Hudson's theorem: a PURE state has nonnegative Wigner function exactly when it is Gaussian; mixed states break the equivalence.

S7.r: Classical-classical (zero-discord) states are a strict subcluster of separable states - generic separable states are already discordant.

S8.r: Thermal states carry zero energy coherence by definition - the state-side resource for thermodynamic contextuality witnesses is absent.

S9.r: Odd-d stabilizer states all have nonnegative (Gross) Wigner functions - the negativity witness is blind on the whole cluster.

S10.r: Bound (PPT) entangled states are the entangled subcluster on which the PPT test is blind and distillation fails.

P1.r: Thermal operations are a strict subcluster of covariant (time-symmetric) processes.

P2.r: Covariant processes cannot create energy coherence - they can only degrade asymmetry.

P3.r: LOCC operations cannot create entanglement - they can only degrade it.

P4.r: Incoherent operations cannot create basis coherence.

P5.r: Clifford and Gaussian unitaries are subgroups of the unitaries - each the free reversible dynamics of its own resource theory.

P6.r: Free stabilizer circuits alone are classically simulable: no quantum advantage without injecting magic.

P7.r: Local filters can activate Bell violation from states that were Bell-local before filtering - processes can unlock hidden nonlocality.

P8.r: The TPM protocol's first energy measurement erases input coherence before readout: whatever the state carried, the process hides it.
P8.c: Why coherent work statistics need beyond-TPM protocols.

P9.r: Weak and direct sequential measurements read KD values and weak values without destroying the probed coherence - the process cluster that reveals what TPM hides.

P10.r: Gaussian operations preserve Wigner positivity: negativity cannot be created inside the Gaussian cluster.

P11.r: Non-Gaussian operations (cubic-or-higher generators, photon counting) are what generate Wigner negativity - and are required for CV universality.
P11.c: The process-side face of the Moyal lift (GN5).

N1.r: Time-symmetric probing hides contextuality: covariant dynamics with time-symmetric effects cannot tell any state from its dephased shadow, so the fragment is noncontextual, KD-positive and coherence-blind for EVERY input.
N1.c: Nondegenerate H; degenerate blocks escape (SG1). TPM fluctuation theorems are the special case. Generated, round 2.

N2.r: No state is immune to contextuality witnesses: state-independent sets fire on every state, thermal and maximally mixed included - so contextuality blindness is purely process-side.
N2.c: SI sets are necessarily non-TTS for nondegenerate H (corollary of N1). Generated, round 2.

W1.r: The CHSH functional is the witness of Bell violation (threshold 2); the same functional marks the quantum ceiling (2 sqrt 2) and the PR maximum (4).

W1b.r: Above 2 sqrt 2 the same CHSH functional witnesses superquantum (PR-type) correlations - the recorded exception to one-witness-one-effect.

W2.r: Steering is witnessed by steering inequalities, equivalently the local-hidden-state membership SDP over the steered assemblage.

W3.r: Incompatibility is witnessed by the joint-measurability SDP; incompatibility robustness measures the margin.

W4.r: Entanglement is witnessed by operators W with Tr(W sigma_sep) >= 0 > Tr(W rho) - operationally reached only through a pathway: entangled state, then locally implementable incompatible measurement settings, then the negative witness value.
W4.c: Complete in principle (Hahn-Banach), NP-hard to use universally; see pathways K11/K13/K14/K16/K18.

W5.r: Generalized contextuality is witnessed by noncontextuality inequalities; the complete test is the simplex-embedding linear program on the accessed fragment.

W6.r: State-independent contextuality is witnessed by fixed operator sets (Peres-Mermin, Yu-Oh) violated by every state.
W6.c: The resource is entirely in the measurement set.

W7.r: State-dependent KS contextuality is witnessed by the KCBS pentagon functional - some states violate it, the maximally mixed state does not.

W8.r: Wigner negativity is witnessed pointwise by the displaced-parity estimator (CV) or phase-point operators (odd d).
W8.c: The parity measurement is itself non-Gaussian.

W9.r: KD nonpositivity is witnessed by direct weak-then-strong measurement of the KD distribution; its imaginary part exists only because of the complex unit.

W10.r: Anomalous weak values are witnessed by the postselected weak-measurement protocol - each anomaly certifies contextuality.

W11.r: Anomalous work and heat are witnessed by work-quasiprobability protocols; negativity of the work distribution certifies contextuality of the process.
W11.c: Requires beyond-TPM protocols and energy-coherent states.

W12.r: Magic is witnessed by stabilizer monotones (robustness, mana, extent); mana is blind on Wigner-positive bound magic, robustness is not.

W13.r: Coherence is witnessed by monotones (l1, relative entropy), interference visibility, and event-graph inequalities for basis-independent set coherence.

W14.r: Discord is witnessed by the failure of local broadcasting: copyable iff zero discord.

W15.r: No-broadcasting is witnessed by cloning-fidelity bounds: the certified impossibility of beating 5/6 (qubits) is the detection.

W16.r: Two-path interference is witnessed by fringe visibility - but visibility alone does NOT certify nonclassicality: epistricted theories reproduce it.

W17.r: Higher-order interference is witnessed by the Sorkin I3 estimator - identically zero throughout quantum theory, so in practice a null test.
